title: Cocktail 2 Is the Most Wanted Film in India Right Now. Next Friday, We Find Out If It Deserves to Be.
excerpt: Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon, and Rashmika Mandanna lead Bollywood's hottest love triangle into theaters on June 19 — and IMDb says nothing else in India comes close.
body:
The numbers arrived first. Before the reviews, before the opening-day chaos, before anyone knew whether **Cocktail 2** would live up to a legacy or collapse under the weight of it — the numbers showed up and made the argument themselves.

<youtube></youtube>

IMDb's real-time most-anticipated rankings, which track page views and user engagement across every upcoming Indian release, put Cocktail 2 at number one. Not close to number one. Not neck-and-neck. It commands a 21% page view share — nearly triple the next Hindi film on the list. **Akshay Kumar**'s Welcome To The Jungle, releasing a week later with a cast sheet that reads like a reunion tour, sits at 7%. The gap is staggering.

So what's driving it? Start with the cast.

## The Triangle

**Shahid Kapoor** plays Kunal. **Kriti Sanon** is Ally. **Rashmika Mandanna** is Diya. The trailer, which dropped on June 2 and hasn't left anyone's timeline since, introduces three people who start as friends and end up in the kind of romantic wreckage that makes for either a great film or a very expensive therapy session.

> "Cocktail 2 is what summer feels like. It has madness, emotion, humour, romance and a lot of heart." — Shahid Kapoor

Shahid reunites with Kriti after the surprise success of *Teri Baaton Mein Aisa Uljha Jiya*, and the chemistry is immediate — loose, warm, flirtatious without being forced. Rashmika, making her biggest Bollywood play yet, slots into the dynamic with a vulnerability that the trailer uses sparingly and effectively. You see it in a single shot: Diya watching Kunal and Ally laugh together, her smile not quite reaching her eyes.

Kriti, for her part, described the characters as "beautifully flawed." Rashmika called it "a beautiful mix of love, friendship and all the emotions that come with figuring life out." Director **Homi Adajania**, who helmed the 2012 original, went further: "Funny, messy, emotional and a little reckless."

That tracks. The trailer has an urban, sun-drenched energy — **Sicily** in one frame, Delhi in the next, Chandigarh somewhere in between — and it leans into the mess. These aren't people who have their lives figured out. They're people who think they do, which is always more interesting.

## The Music Factor

The original *Cocktail* was as much a soundtrack as a film. "Tumhi Ho Bandhu," "Daaru Desi," "Luttna" — those songs defined a generation of house parties and long drives. The sequel knows this.

**Pritam Chakraborty** returns as music director, with lyrics by **Amitabh Bhattacharya**. Two tracks have already surfaced: *Mashooka*, an energetic romantic number shot across Sicilian coastlines that plays like a glossy music video brought to life, and *Tujhko*, a gut-punch of a ballad sung by **Arijit Singh** that centers Shahid and Rashmika's emotional arc. At a media preview, *Tujhko* reportedly left journalists in silence — the kind of reaction that doesn't happen for generic love songs.

The music strategy is smart. By the time the film opens, audiences will already know the songs. They'll walk into theaters humming. That's not marketing. That's muscle memory.

## What the Box Office Expects

Trade analysts are projecting an opening day of ₹9-11 crore net at the Indian box office, which would make Cocktail 2 potentially the **fourth-biggest opening for a Bollywood rom-com since COVID**. For context, the original opened at around ₹5.5 crore in 2012 — a different era, but the trajectory tells a story.

**Maddock Films** and **Luv Films** are co-producing, a partnership that combines Dinesh Vijan's instinct for crowd-pleasers with **Luv Ranjan**'s grip on modern romance. Ranjan co-wrote the story and serves as creative lead, which explains the trailer's tonal confidence. The screenplay is by **Ritesh Shah**, whose credits include *Pink* and *Kaabil* — not exactly rom-com territory, but exactly the kind of writer who gives romantic stories structural bones.

## The Diaspora Equation

For NRIs, the timing is almost suspiciously perfect. June 19 falls on a Friday — opening night lined up perfectly with the weekend to dissect every plot twist over chai. The film will release wide across North America, the UK, and the Gulf — Maddock has been aggressive about international prints since *Stree 2*'s overseas breakout last year.

The original *Cocktail* hit differently for diaspora audiences. Deepika's Veronica wasn't just a character; she was every second-generation kid who'd been told they were too Western, too free, too much. If the sequel finds even half that cultural nerve, it won't just be a hit. It'll be a conversation.

Costume designer **Anaita Shroff Adajania** — who also dressed the original — is handling the fashion, which means expect the looks to generate as much social media heat as the plot. The Sicily sequences alone, judging from the trailer's color palette of burnt oranges and Mediterranean blues, look like they were styled for Instagram before they were styled for cinema.

## The Verdict Before the Verdict

A week out, Cocktail 2 has everything a Bollywood blockbuster needs: star power, nostalgia, music that sticks, and a trailer that people actually want to rewatch. Whether it delivers on the promise is another question — sequels to beloved films carry a particular kind of pressure, and the original's magic was partly accidental, partly lightning.

But here's the thing. The film that sits at number one on IMDb's anticipation chart, that has trade analysts adjusting forecasts upward, that has three of Bollywood's most bankable faces at the peak of their appeal — that film doesn't need to be perfect. It needs to be *felt*.

June 19. Mark it.
